profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal troubleshooting meeting in an ML research lab working on reproducing and extending an MS-SSIDEC-style pipeline for bearing fault diagnosis on a new industrial vibration dataset. Over the last week, the team has seen inconsistent stage-two behavior: one run appears to 'collapse' after SSIDEC fine-tuning, while another run produces usable clusters but poor downstream pseudo-label gains. The agenda is to compare what each person observed, diagnose whether the issue comes from the labeled-sample protocol, stage-two training, or pseudo-label selection, and agree on one concrete rerun plan before the next experiment cycle. The expected outcome is a shared troubleshooting plan for the next run, including what checkpoint to restart from and how to evaluate whether the issue is fixed.

members.name: Dr. Lina Zhao
members.role: Postdoctoral Researcher in Semi-Supervised Representation Learning
members.expertise: Deep clustering, semi-supervised learning, representation learning for time-series fault diagnosis
members.background: Lina leads the algorithm side of the project and adapted the SCCAE+SSIDEC+VAT pipeline from the paper into the lab's PyTorch codebase; she usually works from notebook-based analyses of embedding geometry and cluster assignments.
members.private_state: She wants to show that the core method is sound and that the current instability is a reproducibility detail rather than a fundamental flaw in the approach, because she is preparing an internal report and possible workshop submission.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the '2% labeled setting,' it means 2% of all training windows after the standard sliding-window extraction, regardless of operating condition balance.
When someone says stage two 'collapsed,' they mean the clustering dynamics degenerated visibly in the embedding space or cluster occupancy, even before looking at downstream classifier performance.
A 'checkpoint rerun' naturally means restarting from the SCCAE encoder checkpoint saved right after unsupervised pretraining and before any SSIDEC/VAT updates.
Using 'high-confidence pseudo labels' means applying one absolute confidence threshold to every unlabeled window, with no per-cluster quota.
If preprocessing is said to be 'the same as baseline,' that implies the lab's default per-window normalization convention.

members.name: Arun Patel
members.role: Research Engineer for ML Experimentation and Data Pipelines
members.expertise: Experiment tracking, dataset preparation, scalable training pipelines, signal preprocessing for industrial monitoring
members.background: Arun maintains the data loaders, experiment configs, and run registry for the bearing-fault project; he translated the original paper's setup into reproducible YAML configs and monitors downstream diagnosis accuracy and pseudo-label quality.
members.private_state: He wants to prevent another week of invalid reruns caused by inconsistent experiment bookkeeping, and he is more concerned with whether the final diagnosis model improves than with whether the intermediate clusters look elegant.
hidden_assumptions: The '2% labeled setting' means 2% of the labeled budget at the condition-balanced group level after the sampling script enforces equal counts per fault type and speed-load regime.
If stage two 'collapsed,' that means the pseudo labels produced after SSIDEC are no longer useful for augmenting the supervised set, even if cluster plots still look reasonable.
A 'checkpoint rerun' means resuming from the tracked experiment artifact that already includes the exact stage-two state used in the failing run, so that comparisons remain apples-to-apples.
Selecting 'high-confidence pseudo labels' should be done relative to each predicted cluster, otherwise dominant clusters will swamp the augmented set.
When the team says preprocessing is 'the same as baseline,' that means the globally fit normalization stored with the training split in the pipeline config.

misalignment_points.topic: What the '2% labeled setting' is a percentage of
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to reproducing the '2% labeled setting' from the paper-style protocol.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means 2% of all extracted training windows after windowing, taken from the train split without further balancing by condition.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means 2% of a condition-balanced labeled budget determined after grouping by fault category and operating regime, which yields a different effective number of windows.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In the lab, '2%' is used as shorthand because everyone assumes the sampling script and the analysis notebook refer to the same labeled pool; the difference only lives in how the percentage is operationalized inside separate tools.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether stage two is 'collapsing' and whether the run is 'fixed.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 judges collapse by internal clustering behavior: centroid drift, one-cluster dominance, or visibly compressed embeddings during SSIDEC optimization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 judges collapse by downstream utility: pseudo-label precision and whether the final diagnosis model improves after augmentation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards are plausible in a troubleshooting meeting, and 'collapse' sounds like an obviously shared technical diagnosis, so neither notices that one is using an intermediate-state criterion while the other is using an end-task criterion.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'checkpoint' they mean to rerun from
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'rerun from the checkpoint' to isolate the issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the SCCAE encoder checkpoint saved after stage-one pretraining and before cluster-center initialization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the tracked run artifact saved during stage two after VAT was already active, because that is the checkpoint attached to the problematic experiment record.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There are multiple standard checkpoints in the pipeline, but the team usually says 'the checkpoint' in conversation because each person is anchored to the artifact they most often inspects; the singular phrasing creates false consensus.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both propose tightening 'high-confidence pseudo labels' before the third stage.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means keep every unlabeled window whose maximum assignment probability exceeds a single global threshold, across all clusters and time segments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means select only the top-ranked windows within each predicted cluster and exclude transition segments flagged by the segmentation pipeline, even if some discarded windows exceed the global threshold.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both approaches are commonly described as using 'high-confidence' pseudo labels, and the omitted boundary details feel like implementation defaults rather than decisions important enough to restate in a short troubleshooting meeting.

turns.inner_thought: I need to frame this as a stage-two stability issue, not a fundamental problem with the SCCAE+SSIDEC idea. In the 2% labeled setting, using 2% of all train windows after sliding-window extraction, the encoder looked fine right after unsupervised pretraining. The trouble starts once SSIDEC optimization begins: in my notebook, the embeddings compress and cluster assignments start to look unhealthy before I even care about the classifier. If I emphasize that sequence clearly, it supports the argument that the core method is still sound.
turns.utterance: From what I saw, the latest MS-SSIDEC reproduction in the 2% labeled setting was actually pretty stable through SCCAE pretraining, and then stage two started collapsing. So I don't think the first stage is where the instability is coming from.

turns.inner_thought: I did look at the same 2% labeled setting, meaning the balanced labeled budget after the sampling script enforced equal counts by fault type and operating regime. From my side, the bigger problem is that even when stage two looked finished in the tracked run, the pseudo labels were not good enough to improve the final diagnosis model. I need to keep this discussion grounded in a reproducible outcome, not just whether the intermediate plots look nice.
turns.utterance: I was looking at that same 2% labeled setting run, and from the pipeline side the thing that stood out wasn't just stage two itself. The real issue was that the pseudo-label augmentation still didn't help, even after stage two had supposedly converged.

turns.inner_thought: He may be focusing too much on the end metric. In my embedding analysis, once VAT ramps up, one centroid begins pulling in most of the windows and the representation geometry visibly compresses. To me that's already collapse, regardless of whether some downstream number later looks passable. I should point to the internal dynamics without overexplaining the implementation details.
turns.utterance: Right, but the embedding plots make me think the failure starts earlier than the augmentation step. As soon as VAT really ramps up, one centroid starts attracting most of the points, and that's where it looks like stage two is already collapsing.

turns.inner_thought: Her notebook view and my registry view are not telling the same story, but I don't want another loose discussion without a clean rerun. In the experiment tracker, cluster occupancy didn't look obviously broken, but pseudo-label precision was poor and the downstream gains disappeared. The cleanest way to isolate VAT is to resume from the tracked stage-two artifact attached to that failing run, because otherwise we won't have an apples-to-apples comparison.
turns.utterance: That's interesting, because in the run registry I don't see anything obviously disastrous in the occupancy summaries, but I do see poor pseudo-label quality. Maybe the cleanest thing is to rerun from the checkpoint and see whether VAT is actually the culprit.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, rerun from the checkpoint makes sense—as long as that means the SCCAE encoder checkpoint right after unsupervised pretraining, before any SSIDEC or VAT updates. That way the cluster initialization and the labeled subset are held fixed, and we can test whether stage two itself destabilizes things. I should stress keeping the same initialization with labeled data so the comparison stays clean.
turns.utterance: I agree, let's rerun from the checkpoint. We should keep the same initialization with labeled data so the comparison stays clean and we can isolate whether the stage-two behavior is what changed.

turns.inner_thought: Before I relaunch anything, I need to make sure nobody has quietly drifted off the balanced sampling setup. In my configs, the 2% labeled setting is derived from the condition-balanced budget, and the balanced sampling config was unchanged relative to the earlier baseline. If Lina's notebook used a different labeled pool, that would explain a lot—but right now she sounds like we're aligned, so I'll just confirm the config on my side.
turns.utterance: Before we relaunch, I want to verify the labeled budget in the 2% labeled setting. As far as the configs go, the balanced sampling setup was unchanged from the earlier baseline, so I just want to make sure we're still comparing like with like.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds fine. For stage three, the safest adjustment is to be stricter with pseudo labels so noisy assignments don't contaminate the classifier. In my mind that means a single higher confidence threshold applied to all unlabeled windows after stage two, with no extra quotas or filtering logic. If the method is stable, that alone should protect the diagnosis model enough for the report.
turns.utterance: And for the third stage, I'd like to make the pseudo-labeling stricter. We should only use high-confidence pseudo labels so the diagnosis model doesn't get poisoned by noisy assignments.

turns.inner_thought: Good, I can tighten high-confidence pseudo labels in the pipeline—but I definitely want cluster-aware selection so the dominant predicted group doesn't swamp the augmented set, and I also want to preserve coverage after the segmentation filters remove transition segments. She probably just means the same practical thing from the algorithm side, so no need to belabor it now.
turns.utterance: Yeah, that makes sense. I can tighten the high-confidence pseudo labels in the pipeline while still preserving cluster coverage, so we don't end up dropping a fault type from the augmented set.

turns.inner_thought: If the rerun from the SCCAE checkpoint no longer shows the same centroid drift and compressed embedding geometry, then I can credibly call this a stage-two stability bug rather than evidence against the method. That's important for the internal report and the workshop draft. I should summarize it in those terms.
turns.utterance: So to summarize: if the rerun no longer collapses, I think we should treat this as a stage-two stability bug rather than a problem with the method itself.

turns.inner_thought: I'll relaunch tonight from the tracked stage-two checkpoint under the same balanced 2% labeled setting and compare pseudo-label precision plus final diagnosis accuracy tomorrow. If those improve, I can call the fix held. Hopefully this time the bookkeeping stays airtight and we don't burn another week on mismatched reruns.
